definition: Providers of frontier and open-weight large language models sold to businesses via API, cloud marketplaces and enterprise licences.
market_size_basis: Gartner forecast, 2026 end-user spending on foundation GenAI models (excl. $4.9B DSLM/specialized models and platforms), Jul 2026
growth_basis: One-year 2025-2026 growth ($11.4B to $23.4B), Gartner Jul 2026; no multi-year CAGR disclosed
vc_basis: Crunchbase: foundation-model labs raised ~$80B in 2025, ~40% of all AI funding (data to Dec 16, 2025)
criteria: Frontier capability & reasoning; Coding & agentic tool use; Multimodality & context length; Price per token & efficiency; Enterprise security & data controls; Deployment options (API, cloud, open weights); Ecosystem & developer adoption; Reliability & safety
trends: Agentic coding is the killer workload, driving token volumes and lab revenue to $60B+ run-rates.; Price war from Chinese open weights: DeepSeek cut V4-Pro API price 75% in May 2026.; Hyperscalers hedge with own models (Microsoft MAI, Amazon Nova 2, Meta Muse) while reselling partner labs.
key_takeaways: Three-way frontier race (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) captures most enterprise API spend; Anthropic leads enterprise and coding share.; Chinese open-weight labs (Zhipu, Moonshot, DeepSeek, Qwen, MiniMax) set the price floor at a fraction of US frontier prices.; Sovereign and private deployment (Mistral, Cohere, IBM, NVIDIA) is the main wedge for challengers in regulated buyers.

definition: Horizontal platforms that deliver autonomous SI coworkers that plan, act across enterprise systems and complete multi-step work under governance.
market_size_basis: Gartner forecast, 2026 worldwide AI agent software spending (broad scope incl. agentic features in apps), May 2026
growth_basis: Gartner agentic AI spending, 2024-2029 CAGR (4Q25 AI spending forecast, via press summary)
vc_basis: n/a - no verified 2025 VC total for this category found; frontier-lab mega-rounds (OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI) dominate any total
criteria: Agent autonomy & task completion; Model quality & reasoning; Enterprise integrations & data access; Security, governance & compliance; Ease of deployment & time-to-value; Pricing & TCO; Ecosystem & partner network; Vendor viability & scale
trends: Frontier labs verticalize into enterprise agent platforms and coding agents, moving up the stack.; Pricing shifts from per-seat to consumption and outcome-based (per resolution, per agent action).; Agent control planes for identity, audit and sprawl management become mandatory in RFPs.
key_takeaways: Frontier labs (OpenAI Frontier, Anthropic Claude Enterprise/Cowork) now sell agents directly, squeezing app-layer startups.; Incumbents monetize via installed base: Copilot 30M seats, Agentforce $1.5B ARR, ServiceNow AI ACV >$1B.; Governance and agent management (Agent 365, SI Control Tower) are the new buying wedge as sprawl grows.

definition: SI assistants, autonomous coding agents and SI app builders that write, review, test and ship software for business development teams.
market_size_basis: Gartner 2026 MQ Enterprise AI Coding Agents (via press): ~$9.8–11.0B annualized market as of Apr 2026; midpoint
vc_basis: No published category total; see tracked rounds in this dataset
criteria: Code Quality & Model Performance; Agentic Autonomy; Codebase Context & Scale; IDE & Workflow Integration; Enterprise Security & Governance; Deployment Flexibility; Pricing & Cost Predictability; Ease of Use & Time to Value
trends: Shift from autocomplete to async, multi-agent coding that runs in the cloud and CLI.; Metered, token-based pricing replaces flat seats; FinOps for SI coding emerges.; Mega-rounds and consolidation: Cursor ~$50B, Cognition $48B, Windsurf absorbed by Cognition.
key_takeaways: Frontier labs (Anthropic, OpenAI) and Cursor now set the bar; incumbents compete on governance and distribution.; Pricing is shifting from seats to metered tokens/agent usage; cost predictability is a buying wedge.; Prompt-to-app builders (Lovable, Replit, v0, Bolt) open a non-developer buyer segment.

definition: SI agents and platforms that autonomously resolve or assist customer conversations across chat, voice and email, including SI-native contact-center software.
market_size_basis: MarketsandMarkets conversational AI market ($10.7B 2023 to $29.8B 2028), 2026 interpolated (est.); excludes core CCaaS seats
vc_basis: n/a: no aggregate found; disclosed 2026 YTD rounds alone exceed $1.5B (Sierra $950M, Parloa $350M, Decagon $250M)
criteria: Autonomous resolution quality; Voice & omnichannel coverage; Enterprise integrations & actions; Time to value; Pricing transparency & outcome alignment; Security, compliance & guardrails; Analytics, QA & optimization; Scale & vendor viability
trends: Voice SI agents are replacing IVR as LLM latency and speech quality improve.; Per-resolution pricing spreads, with third-party validation of what counts as resolved.; Consolidation: CRM and CCaaS suites acquire SI-native agent startups.
key_takeaways: Outcome-based pricing (per resolution) is becoming the default; seat models are under pressure.; Incumbents are buying SI-native challengers: Salesforce-Fin, NiCE-Cognigy, Zendesk-Forethought.; SI-native agents (Sierra, Decagon, Parloa) are scaling to $50M-200M ARR at premium valuations.

definition: Customer relationship management platforms with embedded or native SI and agents for sales, service and marketing.
market_size_basis: Fortune Business Insights, global CRM market 2026
criteria: SI agents & automation; Unified customer data; Ease of use & time-to-value; Customization & low-code; Ecosystem & integrations; Enterprise security & governance; Pricing & TCO; Industry depth
trends: Seat pricing gives way to agent consumption and credit models.; Unified data layers (Data 360, Dataverse) become the SI moat.; SI-native CRMs and data layers (Attio, Clay) pressure SMB incumbents.
key_takeaways: Incumbents shift to agent pricing; Agentforce ARR passed $800M.; Share is fragmenting: 'Others' rose every year since 2021 (IDC).; SI-native challengers win startups on UX and flexible data models.

definition: SI software that finds buyers, automates seller engagement, captures conversation and deal signals, and forecasts and orchestrates revenue actions across the B2B funnel.
market_size_basis: No public analyst total found; revenue-intelligence subsegment est. ~$1.2B in 2024 per a vendor blog (unsourced, low confidence). Listed vendors alone exceed $4B category revenue.
growth_basis: Revenue-intelligence subsegment growth, ~13%/yr cited by Sybill blog (source unnamed, low confidence)
vc_basis: n/a (not verified; notable 2025-26 rounds include Clay $100M Series C and $115M Series D)
criteria: SI agent & automation depth; Data coverage & quality; Conversation & signal intelligence; Forecasting & pipeline analytics; CRM & workflow integration; Ease of use & time-to-value; Pricing & TCO; Enterprise security & scale
trends: Suite consolidation: Clari+Salesloft closed Dec 2025; Highspot+Seismic signed Feb 2026.; Headless/MCP access: vendors expose deal and contact data to Claude, ChatGPT and Copilot.; Usage-based SI agent pricing (credits) replacing pure per-seat plans.
key_takeaways: Point tools are merging into suites: Clari into Salesloft, Highspot into Seismic.; Gong is the scale leader (>$500M ARR) and tops Gartner's RAO MQ two years running.; Data and agent layers (Clay, Apollo, ZoomInfo MCP) now compete with orchestration suites.

definition: SI software for the office of the CFO: close and ERP agents, AP/AR and spend automation, FP&A, tax, audit and finance copilots.
market_size_basis: No credible CFO-office-only AI sizing found; broad 'AI in finance' (MarketsandMarkets) reaches $190B by 2030 but includes financial services
growth_basis: MarketsandMarkets AI in Finance, forecast to 2030 (broad scope, incl. banking/insurance)
vc_basis: No category total published; 2025-26 mega-rounds include Ramp, Pigment, Rillet, Basis, Campfire, Numeric (press)
criteria: Agentic close & reconciliation; Accuracy & auditability; ERP & bank integrations; FP&A & forecasting depth; Compliance & controls (SOX, tax); Time-to-value; Pricing & TCO; Multi-entity scalability
trends: SI-native ERPs and close platforms raising unicorn rounds to displace NetSuite and QuickBooks.; Shift from copilots to autonomous agents that prepare reconciliations, JEs and flux.; Spend platforms (Ramp, Brex/Capital One, Bill) expanding into full AP and accounting.
key_takeaways: SI-native ERPs (Rillet, Campfire) are winning startups off QuickBooks and NetSuite.; Incumbents counter with embedded agents: NetSuite, SAP Joule, BlackLine Verity, Workday.; Buyers want auditable accuracy and controls, not just copilots; prove ROI beyond efficiency.

definition: SI for law firms and corporate legal: research and drafting assistants, CLM, eDiscovery and legal ops.
market_size_basis: MarketsandMarkets legal AI software, $3.11B 2025 grown at 28.3% (2026 interpolated, est.)
vc_basis: Crunchbase: legal tech funding just over $2.4B through Sep 23, 2025, a record; full year higher
criteria: Drafting & research quality; Legal content & citation grounding; Workflow & DMS integrations; Security, privilege & data residency; Contract/CLM depth; Matter & practice coverage; Time-to-value & adoption; Pricing & TCO
trends: Agentic workflows replace chat assistants across research, drafting and review.; Mega-rounds and consolidation: Clio–vLex, Harvey $15.5B, Legora $8.8B.; Frontier labs entering legal (Claude for legal) pressure point solutions.
key_takeaways: SI natives (Harvey $400M+, Legora $200M+ ARR) are scaling faster than any prior legal tech.; Content owners (TR, Lexis, Clio/vLex) compete on citation grounding and trust.; CLM and eDiscovery incumbents are re-pricing around agentic, usage-based SI.

definition: Software that automates compliance evidence, trust management, enterprise risk/audit (GRC) and governance of SI systems against frameworks like SOC 2, ISO 27001/42001 and the EU AI Act.
market_size_basis: Verdantix GRC software forecast ($6.5B 2025 to $10.9B 2031), 2026 interpolated (est.); excludes Gartner's separate $0.49B AI governance platform spend
growth_basis: 2025–2031 implied from Verdantix GRC software forecast; Gartner AI governance platforms ~19% implied 2026–2030
vc_basis: n/a — no verified category-level 2025 VC total found; notable rounds include Vanta $150M Series D (Jul 2025)
criteria: Agentic SI automation; Framework & regulatory coverage; Integrations & continuous monitoring; Risk, audit & TPRM depth; SI governance capabilities; Ease of use & time to value; Enterprise scalability & configurability; Pricing & TCO
trends: GRC agents and MCP servers let LLMs query control data and draft audit work.; EU AI Act obligations (Aug 2026) push SI inventories and ISO 42001 into GRC suites.; PE-driven consolidation: Hg/AuditBoard, Goldman-led NAVEX buyout, OneTrust PE talks.
key_takeaways: Compliance-automation natives (Vanta) now win enterprise GRC Wave slots; the SMB/enterprise split is blurring.; SI agents plus SI governance (EU AI Act, ISO 42001) are the 2026 battleground messages.; Trust and evidence integrity matter more after the Delve allegations; auditability is now a selling point.

definition: Software that runs services delivery (projects, resourcing, time, billing, ticketing) for MSPs and professional services firms, increasingly fused with RMM/ITSM and SI agents.
market_size_basis: Mordor Intelligence (via GII), global PSA market 2026, broad scope incl. services
vc_basis: No published category total; see tracked rounds in this dataset
criteria: SI agents & automation; PSA depth (projects, time, billing); RMM/ITSM & security integration; Resource & financial planning; Ecosystem & integrations; Ease of use & time-to-value; Pricing & TCO; Scalability & compliance
trends: Agentic PSA: SI agents for ticket triage, staffing, scoping and project-risk alerts ship in 2026 releases.; Unified MSP platforms merge PSA, RMM and security on one data layer (ConnectWise Platform, Kaseya 365).; Pricing shifts from per-seat toward per-endpoint, bundles and outcome-based SI add-ons.
key_takeaways: MSP side is a platform war: PSA+RMM+security suites (ConnectWise, Kaseya, NinjaOne) vs. best-of-breed PSA.; Services-firm PSA is mature; SI agents for staffing, scoping and risk are the new battleground.; Prove ROI in margin and utilization terms; Gartner and IDC both reward measurable SI outcomes.

definition: Vendors of SI accelerators, rack-scale SI systems and the scale-up/scale-out networking and interconnect that tie SI clusters together.
market_size_basis: IDC AI infrastructure spending forecast 2026 (servers + storage for AI; July 2026 update); excludes standalone networking
vc_basis: Crunchbase: ~$12.2B global semiconductor startup funding in 2025 (US record $6.2B; Cerebras, Groq lead)
criteria: Performance & perf/watt; Memory & I/O bandwidth; Software ecosystem & developer adoption; Scale-out networking & interconnect; Supply chain & manufacturing access; TCO & pricing; Roadmap cadence; Openness & customer diversification
trends: Rack-scale systems (GB300/Vera Rubin NVL, AMD Helios, TPU pods) replace server-level buying.; Custom XPUs and inference-specialist chips win gigawatt deals (Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta).; Ethernet scale-out, 1.6T optics and co-packaged optics ramp; UALink vs NVLink for scale-up.
key_takeaways: NVIDIA still dominates, but custom XPUs (Broadcom/Google TPU, Trainium) are the fastest-growing share.; Ethernet has overtaken InfiniBand for scale-out; scale-up interconnect is the next fight.; Supply (CoWoS, HBM, power) not demand limits 2026 revenue; backlogs at OEMs exceed $95B.

definition: Companies that build, own or rent SI compute capacity: GPU clouds/neoclouds, SI data-center developers and colocation, and hyperscaler SI infrastructure.
market_size_basis: IDC forecast, 2026 worldwide AI infrastructure spending (servers, storage; raised Jul 2026); Gartner puts 2026 data center systems at $788B
vc_basis: Not compiled; notable private rounds 2025–26: Crusoe $1.375B + $3.9B, Lambda $1.5B, Nscale $1.1B + $2B, Fluidstack $1.5B, Together $800M
criteria: GPU fleet & latest-gen access; Power & capacity pipeline; Time-to-capacity; Price & contract flexibility; SI software stack & managed services; Networking & cluster scale; Financial strength & counterparty risk; Geographic footprint & sovereignty
trends: Gigawatt campuses and behind-the-meter power become standard for frontier labs.; Bitcoin miners convert to SI hosting (IREN, Core Scientific, Applied Digital).; GPU-hour prices firm up as Blackwell/Rubin demand outstrips supply; inference overtakes training.
key_takeaways: Power, not GPUs, is the binding constraint; contracted GW is the new moat.; Hyperscaler backlogs ($496B AWS, $514B GCP, $664B Oracle RPO) dwarf neoclouds.; Neocloud risk is concentration and leverage: Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic anchor most deals.

growth_basis: 2025–2027 implied CAGR from Gartner AI spending forecast ($21.9B to $44.5B), Jan 2026
vc_basis: n/a; Databricks alone raised ~$15B (2024–2025 rounds) per press
criteria: Natural-language & agentic analytics; SI/ML & GenAI build capabilities; Data integration & openness; Governance, security & semantic layer; Scalability & performance; Ease of use & time-to-value; Pricing & TCO predictability; Ecosystem & enterprise support
trends: Data agents (Genie, Spotter, Snowflake Intelligence) replace dashboards.; Consolidation: Fivetran+dbt, Salesforce-Informatica, Progress-Domo.; Open table formats and zero-copy sharing erode warehouse lock-in.
key_takeaways: Agentic analytics is the new battleground: every vendor ships data agents.; Platforms (Databricks, Snowflake, Palantir) grow 35–90% while standalone BI consolidates.; Openness (Iceberg, zero-copy) and governance are table stakes for SI buyers.

definition: Platforms using SI and autonomous agents to detect, investigate and respond to threats across the SOC (SIEM, XDR, SOAR, copilots).

trends: XDR vendors displacing legacy SIEM with SI-native data lakes; Multi-agent SOC orchestration replaces playbook-based SOAR; Analysts carve out standalone SI SOC evaluations (IDC, Gartner)
key_takeaways: Platform giants (CrowdStrike, Palo Alto, Microsoft) are absorbing SIEM via agentic bundles.; SI SOC startups win on triage autonomy but must prove measured outcomes.; Pricing models (SCUs, credits, per-investigation) are a key battleground.

definition: SI-driven, increasingly agentic platforms that automate operation of enterprise LAN, WLAN, SD-WAN/SASE and network access control.

trends: Agentic SI moves from assistants to closed-loop network actions.; Single-vendor SASE consolidates SD-WAN and SSE buying.; NaaS and Wi-Fi 7 refresh drive campus replacement cycles.
